results: 1. Comprehensive neurological examination including cranial nerves, motor, sensory, reflexes, coordination, gait, and fundoscopy.
cranial nerve examination: bilateral abduction limitation, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
muscle tone examination: normal
limb strength (MRC) examination: mild distal limb weakness
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: reduced or absent reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): distal loss of vibration and proprioception
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
fundoscopy: normal
2. MRI of the brain and spine with gadolinium contrast.
MRI cervical and thoracic spine: normal
MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
MRI spine: symmetrical thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots
3. Serum acetylcholine receptor antibody test.
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
4. Serum anti-GQ1b antibody test.
not performed / not available
5. Nerve conduction studies and electromyography of the lower extremities.
nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
needle electromyography: chronic neurogenic changes
6. If inconclusive, lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal fluid analysis.
CSF opening pressure: normal
CSF cell count and differential: normal
CSF protein: mildly raised at 73 mg/dL
CSF glucose: normal
lumbar puncture / CSF: protein mildly raised at 73 mg/dL
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) with cranial nerve hypertrophy and enhancement

Alternatives:
1. Hereditary sensory and motor neuropathy (HSMN) with nerve hypertrophy (e.g., Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4)
2. Amyloidosis neuropathy
3. Neurolymphomatosis
